title: Multiplication-tower vanishing detected by localized-module Hom
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $f\in A$, and $K\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $A_f=A[1/f]$ denote the localization of $A$ at $\{1,f,f^2,\ldots\}$, whose elements are fractions $a/f^n$, with $a/f^n=b/f^m$ if and only if $f^r(f^ma-f^nb)=0$ for some $r\geq0$. Regard $A_f$ as an $A$-module complex in degree zero. For any derived limit $T(K,f)$ [def-weil-derived-limit] of the tower with every term $K$ and every transition multiplication by $f$, the following are equivalent: $T(K,f)$ is zero; and $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(A_f[0][q],K)=0$ for every integer $q$. Here a Hom group being zero means that every morphism in it is the zero morphism. No boundedness or nonzerodivisor hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Put P = direct sum over n in N of ULift A, with coprojections i_n. Define d:P -> P by d i_n = i_n - f i_(n+1). Its kernel is zero: the zeroth coefficient of d(x)=0 gives x_0=0, and induction gives x_(n+1)=f*x_n=0. This does not require f to be a nonzerodivisor. The universal property of the sequential colimit identifies its cokernel with colim(A --f--> A --f--> ...): a map annihilating d is exactly a compatible family. Apply [lem-sc-module-localization-filtered-colimit] to ULift A and the canonical localized-module isomorphism to identify this colimit with ULift(A[1/f]). Thus 0 -> P --d--> P -> ULift(A[1/f]) -> 0 is short exact.

proof.text: Apply the degree-zero single-complex functor and the derived localization to this short exact sequence, obtaining a distinguished triangle S(P) --S(d)--> S(P) -> S(ULift(A[1/f])) -> S(P)[1] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The coprojections S(i_n) exhibit S(P) as the coproduct of the S(ULift A), and remain so after any shift. Use the proved source-library declaration DerivedCategory.isColimitCofanMkQObj: it computes maps to a K-injective representative using [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. The required K-injective resolutions exist for the Grothendieck category of modules; the source-library GrothendieckAbelian.KInjectiveResolution supplies them, also after transporting along the ring equivalence ULift A = A to match arbitrary universes.

proof.text: For each integer q, the coproduct universal property identifies maps S(P)[q] -> K with families (g_n) of maps S(ULift A)[q] -> K. Under this identification precomposition by S(d)[q] is (g_n) -> (g_n - f*g_(n+1)). The product universal property identifies postcomposition by the tower Roos endomorphism r=1-shift with precisely the same map on families [def-weil-derived-limit]. Hence the two induced Hom maps are bijective simultaneously. The shifted Yoneda exact sequences of the distinguished triangle in step 2 show that every map S(ULift(A[1/f]))[q] -> K is zero for every q if and only if all these precomposition maps are bijective. Handle the sign in a shifted distinguished triangle by the invertible scalar (-1)^q and use the natural shift-add isomorphisms.

proof.text: The objects S(ULift A)[q] detect isomorphisms in the derived category: by the proved source-library DerivedCategory.singleFunctorZeroHomEquiv, maps from the projective module ULift A in degree zero are maps into zeroth homology; shifting gives every homology degree. Evaluation at 1 identifies module maps from ULift A with elements, so bijectivity of these Hom maps is exactly bijectivity on all homology modules, equivalently an isomorphism by DerivedCategory.isIso_iff. Thus step 3 says the localized-module Hom vanishing is equivalent to r being an isomorphism. Finally hT supplies the distinguished Roos triangle T -> product K --r--> product K -> T[1] [def-weil-derived-limit]; the first object of a distinguished triangle is zero if and only if its second morphism is an isomorphism. This proves the stated equivalence for arbitrary unbounded K and arbitrary f.
